comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (application public API for BEAD-07 CLI; deviations from PLAN BEAD-03):

1. A third module, application/windowed_run.py: WindowedRun(calendar, clock, notifier, window: Window, policy: RetryPolicy), frozen; run(kind: RunKind, attempt: Callable[[], AttemptResult], *, force=False) -> RunReport. AttemptResult(outcome: Outcome, at: datetime, reason: Reason | None = None, screenshot: Path | None = None). Why: the verdict -> decide -> retry -> one-report loop is identical for both use cases (~60 lines); writing it twice would duplicate the rule that holds "exactly one notification per run". Scope deviation: the coordinator named only checkin.py/checkout.py; the new file is inside this bead's own package, which no other wave-2 bead touches.
2. Constructors are not PLAN's MorningCheckin(client, calendar, notifier, clock, artifacts, settings). They are MorningCheckin(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str, hold: timedelta) and EveningCheckout(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str); both .run(*, force=False) -> RunReport. The CLI builds one WindowedRun per kind (checkin window vs checkout window, same calendar/clock/notifier/policy). No Settings: application must not import infrastructure.config, so the CLI unpacks Settings into these values.
3. No ArtifactStore argument: HorizonClient has no screenshot method, the adapter puts the screenshot into HorizonClientError, so the use case had nothing to ask the store. The CLI hands the store to the adapter (as PLAN BEAD-06 already does).
4. application/__init__ re-exports MorningCheckin, EveningCheckout, WindowedRun, AttemptResult.

Contract the use cases rely on from HorizonClient (for BEAD-06 ht-xlh / BEAD-13 probe): (a) desktop_status(name) must work while the desktop is open on #/desktop (RFC: broker XML from the authenticated context; the tile is not on that page); (b) login() is called again after disconnect() closed the browser context, and again on every retry after a failure; (c) checkin calls disconnect() in a finally once open_desktop returned, so it may follow a failed desktop_status.

Mapping decided here: SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY -> SKIPPED/NON_WORKING_DAY; SKIP_LATE and SKIP_EARLY -> SKIPPED/WINDOW_MISSED (only when no attempt was made); GIVE_UP, or a window that closes between retries, -> FAILED with the LAST failure's reason and screenshot. Unconfirmed check-in -> DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN; unconfirmed log off -> LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED; no session at the first look -> SKIPPED/ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, not retried. Any exception other than HorizonClientError from an attempt is a failed attempt with Reason.UNEXPECTED (retried); its message is never logged (type + traceback frames only), because adapter text may quote what it typed. Report time: check-in success = the moment open_desktop returned (before the hold); check-out success = the moment the log off was confirmed; skips/failures = when the run ended.

Known gap (domain, not fixed here): Reason has no member for "started before the window", so SKIP_EARLY renders as "the run started after its window", which is false for an early start. Needs a domain Reason (e.g. WINDOW_NOT_OPEN) and its _REASON_TEXT; owner: coordinator.

Docs to check: docs/domains/application/README.md (sync-check: missing modules checkin, checkout, windowed_run), PLAN.md BEAD-03 and BEAD-07 signatures, RFC.md application table (add windowed_run).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE: new public domain API for BEAD-03 (application) to consume.
- horizon_tracker.domain.calendar: VerdictSource (StrEnum: CALENDAR, WEEKDAY_FALLBACK); WorkingDayVerdict(is_working: bool, source: VerdictSource), frozen; weekday_rule(day: date) -> bool; resolve(calendar_answer: bool | None, day: date) -> WorkingDayVerdict.
- horizon_tracker.domain.schedule: RunKind (StrEnum: CHECKIN="checkin", CHECKOUT="checkout"); Decision (StrEnum: RUN, RETRY, SKIP_EARLY, SKIP_LATE, SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY, GIVE_UP); Window(start: time, end: time), frozen, start < end enforced, contains(moment) with BOTH ends inclusive; RetryPolicy(max_attempts: int >= 1, backoff: timedelta >= 0), frozen; decide(now: datetime, window, verdict, attempt: int (from 1), policy) -> Decision.
DEVIATION FROM PLAN (two extra Decision members): PLAN listed RUN/RETRY/SKIP_LATE/SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY. decide() takes attempt+policy, so it needs an outcome for spent attempts -> GIVE_UP; and a start before the window (07:54:59) must not run and is not 'late' -> SKIP_EARLY. BEAD-03 must handle both (GIVE_UP = failure report 'all attempts failed'; SKIP_EARLY = skip report).
Precedence in decide(): attempt<1 -> ValueError; non-working day -> SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY (even outside the window, so the notice says 'holiday', not 'late'); attempt > max_attempts -> GIVE_UP (even after the window closed); before start -> SKIP_EARLY; after end -> SKIP_LATE; attempt 1 -> RUN; else RETRY.
backoff is a timedelta; the use case passes backoff.total_seconds() to Clock.sleep. now is read as wall time (now.time()), i.e. in the zone the Clock hands out (Europe/Moscow); tzinfo is not converted.
Docs to check: docs/domains/domain/README.md (does NOT name the calendar module -> Gate red, see COMPLETED), RFC.md domain table (decide signature now carries attempt+policy; Decision has 6 members).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (new domain API; two deliberate deviations from PLAN BEAD-02 for BEAD-03..06 to read):
1. session.checkin_succeeded(while_open, after_disconnect) -- PLAN said (before, after). A `before` has no say in check-in success (fresh logon, reconnect and takeover all end the same), so an unused param would have been a lie. The rule is the transition CONNECTED -> DISCONNECTED: Blast was open (logon done), then the client let go without logging off. checkout_succeeded(before, after) as planned: before.has_session and after is NO_SESSION; NO_SESSION->NO_SESSION is NOT success (BEAD-03 reports it as Outcome.SKIPPED + Reason.ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF). SessionState is a StrEnum with a `has_session` property; DesktopStatus(name, state) frozen.
2. Notifier.send(report) -- PLAN said send(report, screenshot=None). RunReport already carries `screenshot`; a second argument would be a second source of truth. The notifier attaches report.screenshot when present.
Other shapes: RunReport(kind: RunKind, outcome: Outcome, at: aware datetime, verdict_source: VerdictSource | None [None = --force, calendar not asked], reason: Reason | None, screenshot: Path | None). `reason` is a closed vocabulary (Reason enum), not free text -- that is what makes "render never contains the password" true by construction; the PLAN wording "reason" as text could not satisfy the password test. Invariants enforced at construction: runtime type checks on every field (TypeError, message never echoes the value), aware `at` (ValueError), reason present iff outcome is not SUCCEEDED (ValueError). render() text is Russian at this point (in the catalogue's English rendering: headline "Check-in succeeded"/"Check-out failed"/..., "Time: dd.mm.yyyy HH:MM:SS MSK", "Calendar: ...", "Reason: ..."); the screenshot is never in the text.
ports.HorizonClientError(reason: Reason, screenshot: Path | None = None); str(error) == reason.value. Adapters (BEAD-06) raise it; use cases (BEAD-03) catch it by name. HorizonClient.login() takes no credentials -- the adapter is constructed with them. probe() -> str (portal version), unreachable = HorizonClientError(PORTAL_UNREACHABLE). Clock.now() returns an aware datetime in the service tz. ArtifactStore.screenshot_path(kind: RunKind) -> Path.
Reason vocabulary: NON_WORKING_DAY, WINDOW_MISSED, ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, PORTAL_UNREACHABLE, LOGIN_REJECTED, DESKTOP_NOT_FOUND, DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN, LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED, UNEXPECTED. Extending it is a domain change (render maps every member; a test fails if one renders empty or duplicates another).
Docs to check: docs/domains/domain/README.md (Responsibilities lists no report module; sync-check flags it stale -- see COMPLETED), PLAN.md BEAD-02/03 signatures, RFC domain table (report "reason" is a closed vocabulary).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (for BEAD-07 ht-oqx, the CLI composition root): horizon_tracker.infrastructure.horizon_playwright

PlaywrightHorizonClient(*, horizon_url: str, username: str, password: str, chrome_path: Path | None, artifacts: ArtifactStore, run_kind: RunKind, timeouts: HorizonTimeouts | None = None)
- Differs from PLAN "PlaywrightHorizonClient(settings, artifacts)". The ctor is keyword-only and does not import infrastructure.config.Settings: that module was still being written in parallel (ht-c5q). The CLI wires it as horizon_url=settings.horizon_url, username=settings.username, password=settings.password, chrome_path=settings.chrome_path, artifacts=<ArtifactStore>, run_kind=RunKind.CHECKIN|CHECKOUT.
- run_kind is new: ArtifactStore.screenshot_path(kind) needs it, and the port methods do not carry it.
- chrome_path=None means Playwright's own bundled Chromium (useful in CI); the VPS passes HT_CHROME_PATH.
- HorizonTimeouts(page_load_ms=30000, action_ms=15000, login_ms=30000, desktop_open_ms=90000, logoff_confirm_ms=60000, poll_ms=1000): frozen dataclass, defaults sized for the live portal.
- Context manager, plus close(). Use `with PlaywrightHorizonClient(...) as client:`. The sync Playwright driver refuses a second instance in the same thread, so close one client before building the next (the CLI's checkin and probe must not overlap in one process).
- probe() -> "HTML Access bundles: <name>, ..." (the <script src> basenames of index.html; no login, no browser launched). Raises PORTAL_UNREACHABLE on a network failure or non-200, and UNEXPECTED when the page names no bundle.
- desktop_status(name): CONNECTED only while this client holds that desktop open. Otherwise it reads the tile: an enabled #menu-item-logoff-btn means DISCONNECTED, a disabled one NO_SESSION. A client that has disconnected logs in again to read it, so checkin can read after_disconnect directly after disconnect().
- log_off(name) on a tile without a session raises ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, and on an unconfirmed log off LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED (after polling the tile).
- Reason mapping: goto/network -> PORTAL_UNREACHABLE; error dialog -> LOGIN_REJECTED; no verdict within login_ms -> UNEXPECTED; no tile -> DESKTOP_NOT_FOUND; signal not reached -> DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN.
Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (lists no horizon_playwright module; sync-check flags it stale), PLAN.md BEAD-06/07 ctor signature, RFC infrastructure table.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: isdayoff.py and telegram.py written test-first (RED by collection error on both, then GREEN). 45 tests in test_isdayoff.py (21) + test_telegram.py (24), 45/45 pass; ruff check + ruff format --check (my 4 files only) + mypy --strict over src and tests clean. tests/unit/infrastructure/__init__.py already existed (created by the neighbour between my mkdir and my check) and was left alone. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (new infrastructure adapters, for BEAD-07 ht-oqx to wire in the CLI):

1. horizon_tracker.infrastructure.isdayoff.IsDayOffCalendar(client: httpx.Client) -- implements WorkingDayCalendar.is_working_day(day: date) -> bool | None. GET https://isdayoff.ru/YYYYMMDD with a per-request timeout of 5 s (TIMEOUT_SECONDS), independent of the client's own default. Body exactly "0"/"2" -> True, "1" -> False. httpx.HTTPError (any transport failure incl. timeouts), status != 200, or any other body (incl. "0\n", "", isdayoff codes 100/101/199) -> None, logged at WARNING on logger horizon_tracker.infrastructure.isdayoff, never raised.

2. horizon_tracker.infrastructure.telegram.TelegramNotifier(token: str, chat_id: str, client: httpx.Client) -- implements Notifier.send(report: RunReport) -> None.
   - report.screenshot is None -> POST bot<token>/sendMessage, form {chat_id, text=render(report)}.
   - report.screenshot set -> POST bot<token>/sendPhoto, multipart {chat_id, caption=render(report), photo=(file name, bytes)}; if the file cannot be read (OSError) or the Bot API refuses/fails the photo, it falls back to sendMessage with the same text, so the owner always gets the report text.
   - Per-request timeout 20 s (TIMEOUT_SECONDS), independent of the client default.
   - Any httpx.HTTPError or non-200 answer is logged at WARNING (method, status, Bot API "description", error type + redacted message) and swallowed: send never raises on delivery.
   - CONSTRUCTOR RAISES ValueError on a malformed token (must fullmatch \d+:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ -- so a trailing newline or space from .env is refused) or an empty/blank chat_id; the message never echoes the value. The CLI should build the notifier at wiring time so a bad secret fails before the run, not mid-run. Strip nothing silently -- the CLI/config decides.
   - Token out of logs: the module logs no URL and redacts the token from error text and descriptions; on construction it attaches (once per process, idempotent) a logging.Filter to the "httpx" logger that masks api.telegram.org/bot<token> as bot<token>-placeholder in httpx's own INFO request lines. Records are never dropped. If the CLI configures logging, it need not silence httpx for the token's sake; httpcore's DEBUG lines carry no URL path.
   - chat_id never appears in my log records either (tested).
Both adapters take the httpx.Client from the caller and never close it: the CLI owns its lifetime (e.g. `with httpx.Client() as client:`).
Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (lists "isdayoff.ru working-day calendar" and "Telegram notifier" as bullets; sync-check now flags it stale against isdayoff.py and telegram.py, hash_changed_since_head), RFC.md infrastructure table (telegram row: add the photo->text fallback and the 20 s timeout), PLAN BEAD-07 wiring.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
COMPLETED: BEAD-05 landed as a7695cd on claude/horizon-vdi-automation-id6b6m (4 files by explicit path, under the merge slot: acquire rc 0, commit, release rc 0; Bead: ht-axc trailer verified via %(trailers:key=Bead,valueonly)). .beads/issues.jsonl and ACTIVE.md left to the coordinator. Not pushed.
What: src/horizon_tracker/infrastructure/{isdayoff,telegram}.py + tests/unit/infrastructure/{test_isdayoff,test_telegram}.py. Both modules annotated # beadloom:domain=infrastructure; the first docstring line names the one responsibility ("Asks the isdayoff.ru production calendar whether a date is a working day." / "Delivers run reports to the owner's Telegram chat through the Bot API."). tests/unit/infrastructure/__init__.py was created by the neighbour (ht-c5q) between my mkdir and my existence check; I left it alone and did NOT commit it -- it is still untracked, for ht-c5q to land. My tests do not need it (clean room below ran without it).
Tests: 45 new (isdayoff 21, telegram 24), 45/45 passed, all on httpx.MockTransport, no network. Tree (with the three neighbours' uncommitted work present): 219 collected / 219 passed; ruff check src/ tests/ clean; mypy src/ (strict) clean; mypy --strict over my tests clean; ruff format applied to my 4 files only.
Clean room (beadloom clean-room ht-axc, HEAD e6df47a + my 4 files, no other carried file): 162 collected / 162 passed (117 HEAD + 45 mine), module __file__ checked to resolve to the room; mypy --strict over room src + my tests clean; ruff clean. The room built no interpreter of its own: the verdict is taken under /home/user/horizon-tracker/.venv/bin/python (the project environment), as the tool states. "Green in a clean room over 4 files" -- a claim about these files, not the combined tree.
Beadloom: in the room on a clean index (rm beadloom.db && reindex): lint --strict rc 0 (only a warn: feature-needs-domain rule_liveness), doctor rc 0; ctx infrastructure lists IsDayOffCalendar and TelegramNotifier. On the tree: sync-check rc 2 -- NOT green: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md is stale (hash_changed_since_head) against isdayoff.py, telegram.py and ht-c5q's artifacts/clock/config.py; application README stale against ht-0jm's files; warn "declared surface grew 9 -> 15 pairs; re-record with --record-surface". The docs are outside this bead's scope -- for the coordinator / tech-writer, as in wave 1. beadloom ci not run green for that reason.
Biting (17 sabotages by targeted reverse edit on my own files, restore checked byte-exact, counts compared, baseline 45 passed, after 45 passed), each red by name: shortened day "2" non-working (test_the_calendar_reads_the_isdayoff_day_code); isdayoff timeout removed (test_the_calendar_gives_isdayoff_five_seconds_and_no_more); status unchecked (test_an_error_status_is_no_answer x5); only timeouts caught (test_a_network_failure_is_no_answer x2); date form %Y%d%m (test_the_calendar_asks_isdayoff_for_the_day_in_its_compact_date_form); body truncated to first char (test_an_unexpected_body_is_no_answer x2); httpx filter not installed (test_no_log_record_from_any_logger_carries_the_token_or_the_chat_id x3); redact identity (same test, network-down + description-echoes-token); screenshot ignored (3 photo tests); no text fallback after refused photo (test_a_photo_the_bot_api_rejects_still_delivers_the_text); refusal raises (7 failed); network error escapes (3); token shape unchecked (test_a_malformed_token_is_refused_without_echoing_it x5); telegram timeout removed (test_the_notifier_gives_the_bot_api_a_bounded_time); caption truncated (photo test); filter drops records instead of masking (test_httpx_request_lines_still_name_the_bot_method + token test); blank chat id accepted (test_an_empty_chat_id_is_refused).
Vacuity found and fixed before sabotage: httpx's default client timeout is itself 5 s, so a timeout test on a default client could not tell the adapter's timeout from the client's. The isdayoff test now builds its client with timeout=60, the Telegram one with timeout=None. One harness bug of mine: the first run computed the restore but did not write it, so isdayoff.py was left with "2": False; caught by the harness's own byte-compare assertion, restored by targeted sed, 45/45 re-verified before the full run.
Decisions: (1) the token leak through httpx's own INFO line "HTTP Request: POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/..." is real for any CLI that logs at INFO; closed in the adapter with an idempotent masking filter on the "httpx" logger rather than by asking the CLI to silence httpx, so the guarantee lives next to the token. The token test captures EVERY logger at DEBUG and asserts records exist, so it cannot pass by silence. (2) Photo -> text fallback: a refused photo (e.g. PHOTO_INVALID_DIMENSIONS on a tall page) must not cost the owner the report text. (3) Token validated at construction (Telegram's <digits>:<secret> shape): a malformed token would otherwise surface as httpx.InvalidURL, whose message carries the URL with the token, at notification time. (4) isdayoff body matched exactly, no strip: an unknown shape falls back to the weekday rule and the fallback is named in the notification.
API changes: see the API CHANGE comment.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (for BEAD-07 cli, ht-oqx): new public infrastructure API, commit 282811b.

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.config
- ConfigError(variable, problem): Exception; .variable = the env var name; str = "<VAR>: <problem>"; never carries a credential value.
- Settings (frozen dataclass), Settings.from_env(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> Settings (pass os.environ; it is not read implicitly). Fields, in order:
  horizon_url: str            <- HORIZON_URL            REQUIRED (no default: deployment-specific, the RFC value is not baked into code)
  username: str               <- HORIZON_USERNAME       REQUIRED, credential (masked)
  password: str               <- HORIZON_PASSWORD       REQUIRED, credential (masked); value kept verbatim, not stripped
  desktop: str                <- HORIZON_DESKTOP        default "DEV desktop"
  telegram_token: str         <- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN     REQUIRED, credential (masked)
  telegram_chat_id: str       <- TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID       REQUIRED, credential (masked); kept as str
  timezone: ZoneInfo          <- HT_TIMEZONE            default Europe/Moscow; unknown key -> ConfigError
  checkin_window: Window      <- HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW      default 07:55-08:00; strict HH:MM-HH:MM -> domain.schedule.Window
  checkout_window: Window     <- HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW     default 17:00-17:05; start >= end -> ConfigError
  hold_seconds: int           <- HT_HOLD_SECONDS        default 120; non-negative whole number (0 allowed)
  chrome_path: Path           <- HT_CHROME_PATH         default /usr/bin/google-chrome
  artifacts_dir: Path         <- HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR       default /opt/horizon-tracker/artifacts
  Blank (whitespace-only) required var = missing; blank optional var = its default.
  repr/str/f-string render '***' for username, password, telegram_token, telegram_chat_id (CONTEXT lists the AD account and chat id as secrets too, so the mask is wider than "password and token").
  Constants exported: MASK, DEFAULT_* (one per optional variable).

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.clock
- SystemClock(tz: ZoneInfo): implements domain.ports.Clock. now() -> aware datetime in tz; sleep(seconds) -> time.sleep (negative raises ValueError).

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.artifacts
- RETENTION = timedelta(days=14)
- DirectoryArtifactStore(directory: Path, clock: Clock, retention: timedelta = RETENTION): implements domain.ports.ArtifactStore.
  screenshot_path(kind: RunKind) -> directory/"YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<kind>.png" by clock wall time; creates the directory, writes no file.
  prune() -> list[Path]: removes files named in that shape whose name time is strictly older than now - retention; foreign files, directories, malformed dates are left alone; absent directory -> []. NOT called implicitly: the CLI composition root should call store.prune() once per run (logs each removal at INFO).
  Same-second collision of the same kind overwrites (one screenshot per failed attempt, attempts are spaced by backoff).

Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (sync-check: "missing modules: artifacts, clock, config"), services/cli.md once BEAD-07 wires these; RFC "API Changes" table could note which vars are required vs defaulted.
